result.title: Motion on Demand: Adaptive Optical Excitation for Event Cameras
result.summary: Event cameras respond only to brightness changes, so whether an edge is visible depends on image motion perpendicular to it---a motion that constantly shifts with camera and scene dynamics. Rotating a wedge prism in front of the lens introduces controlled image motion to reveal static or slow edges. However, a fixed rotation speed cannot adapt to changing motion conditions: when natural motion is already sufficient, additional optical excitation generates redundant events and introduces unnecessary alignment errors. Inspired by the division of labor between fast haltere feedforward and slower visual feedback in fly gaze control, we present EvGaze, an event camera system that adaptively regulates prism rotation speed. EvGaze employs a learned multimodal controller that integrates luminance, event, and inertial observations, with a fast inertial pathway that refines speed decisions between visual updates. To preserve geometric consistency during speed changes, we compensate for prism-induced image motion at individual event timestamps using measured encoder angles. On EvMotion, EvGaze recovers more edges than full-speed prism rotation with 39% fewer events. On DSEC with simulated optical modulation, it reaches 0.73 feature-tracking success (compared with 0.55 on native events and 0.67 at 180 RPM) while generating 26% fewer events than 360 RPM. Real-device experiments further demonstrate online closed-loop adaptation, reducing average event rates by 17% relative to full-speed rotation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 EvGaze：在事件相机前旋转楔形棱镜以引入受控图像运动来显露静态边缘，并用融合亮度、事件与惯性观测的学习型控制器自适应调节棱镜转速，以较少事件保留更多边缘。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按当前运动条件决定是否及以多快速度补充视觉激发」的主动感知策略，以及快惯性前馈通路在两次视觉更新之间精化决策的结构，可能为 LVR 中「何时获取更多视觉证据」与多速率状态更新提供可供核查的启发。
